mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings impact.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in the unemployment rate below 4% signals a labor market so tight that wage inflation will soon accelerate, prompting the Fed to raise rates and depress equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: CPI inflation remains below 2% despite the tight labor market, indicating that the Fed will not feel compelled to tighten policy aggressively.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production growth slows by more than 2% year-over-year, it signals a supply-side slowdown that will crimp corporate profits and lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: ISM manufacturing PMI remains above 55, indicating that the production slowdown is likely to be temporary and not indicative of a broader economic downturn.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 4%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that will slow economic growth and depress equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Real GDP growth accelerates despite the high interest rates, indicating that the economy is resilient to the tightening and that equity valuations may not be as negatively impacted as expected.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts fall by more than 10% year-over-year, it signals a weakening in the housing market that will depress consumer spending and lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 10-year Treasury yield falls below 3%, indicating that mortgage rates are likely to remain low and support housing demand despite the drop in starts.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises by more than 0.5 percentage points over a 3-month period, it signals a weakening labor market that will depress consumer spending and lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Initial jobless claims fall to a new cycle low, indicating that the rise in unemployment is likely to be temporary and not indicative of a broader labor market downturn.

mechanism_narrative: When the spread between the 10-year and 2-year Treasury yields inverts (10y < 2y), it signals a coming recession that will lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The yield curve steepens (10y-2y > 0.5%) within 3 months of inverting, indicating that the recession signal was likely a false positive.

mechanism_narrative: When real retail sales growth slows by more than 2% year-over-year, it signals a weakening consumer sector that will depress corporate profits and lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Consumer confidence rises to a new cycle high, indicating that the slowdown in retail sales is likely to be temporary and not indicative of a broader consumer spending downturn.
